title: The Training Intensity Distribution of Marathon Runners Across Performance Levels
authors: Muniz-Pumares D, Hunter B, Meyler S, Maunder E, Smyth B
population: Training in the 16 weeks before 151,813 marathons completed by 119,452 runners, from recreational to fast (marathon 120-150 min group)
findings: Mean training volume across all runners was 45.1 +/- 26.4 km per week; the fastest runners (marathon 120-150 min) accumulated more than three times the volume of slower runners.
Three-zone model: critical speed is the Z2/Z3 boundary and Z1/Z2 transition assumed at 82.3% of critical speed.

Time in Z2 and Z3 stayed relatively stable across performance levels; the proportion in Z1 was higher in progressively faster groups; pyramidal TID was most common, adopted by more than 80% of the fastest runners.
Marathon time correlated negatively with volume markers and Z1 proportion (p<0.01, R2 >= 0.90); Z2 and Z3 proportions correlated with slower times (R2 >= 0.85).
limitations: Observational group-level correlations; zones derived from critical speed estimated from the same training data; talent and history confounding; slower runners likely run closer to threshold when going easy; reverse causation possible. Crossref online 2024-12; Europe PMC issue year 2025.
implications: Add weekly volume mainly as easy (Z1) running and keep absolute Z2+Z3 time roughly constant; default structure pyramidal.
Use 45 km/week (SD 26) only as a population reference and scale the target to the goal-time band.
Estimate critical speed from logged runs and set Z1/Z2 at 82.3% of it.

verification.notes: Crossref title, journal, first author match; abstract re-fetched and every number matches. Kept at C because the evidence is group-level correlation.
